newsitem.title: UK: Rump Hanson seen valued at 2.3 bln stg-FT.
newsitem.headline: Rump Hanson seen valued at 2.3 bln stg-FT.

text.p: Hanson Plc is likely to be valued at 2.3 billion pounds ($3.85 billion) after its demerger reduced it to a building materials producer, according to research by ABN Amro Hoare Govett, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.

The newspaper said Hoare, Hanson's broker, suggested shares in the aggregates, bricks, cranes and electrical equipment group would be worth 44 pence after a four-way breakup had been completed. Hanson shares closed on Tuesday at 86-1/4 pence.
"The broker's valuation was based upon its forecast pretax profits of 232 million stg for the year to the end of September 1997," the newspaper said.

"The research provides the most detailed picture yet of the financial characteristics of the remaining Hanson business in which Mr Robert Hanson, son of the founder, will play a key role as development director," the article said.
The FT said full details are not expected from Hanson until the end of January when investor presentations in Britain and the United States are planned.
